messages:
Taylor (Support): heads-up — Acme reported a big jump in inference latency p95 for /v1/generate starting ~2026-03-12 14:04 UTC. They say p95 went from ~120ms to ~420ms. Customer attached our dashboard screenshot and csv of samples.
Sam (Oncall): link? can you paste the panel or share the query?
Taylor (Support): https://redwood.internal/d/ops/latency?panelId=7 — screenshot in thread. Panel title says p95 latency (prod, last 24h).
Jordan (Observability): I pulled the panel. Odd — our dashboard p95 (histogram_quantile over aggregations) shows a bump earlier than raw traces. Traces don't show 420ms p95 for that customer.
Taylor (Support): Customer insists their app saw higher tail — they provided sample response times from client side (attached). Those match ~400ms p95.
Sam (Oncall): could be routing -> customer hitting dedicated fallback or cross-region. Alex can you confirm routing policy for that org around that time?
Alex (Eng-SRE): checking routing logs... org-acme was routed to pool-gpu-a in us-west1 until 14:10 then to pool-gpu-b for 10m due to slot pressure. Pool-gpu-b has slightly higher median due to different instance types. That could explain +30-60ms, not +300ms.
Jordan (Observability): one more suspicion — our dashboard panel uses rollup metrics that downsample histograms to 1m buckets and then uses histogram_quantile at query time. If bucket boundaries are coarse, quantile gets "floored" — big jumps can appear when samples fall on different buckets. The customer-sent raw client samples are individual requests, not server-side histograms.
Taylor (Support): so the two sources don't match because we're comparing different aggregations? How do we explain the 400ms?
Sam (Oncall): steps to repro: 1) run a steady load against /v1/generate using same prompt and batch settings as customer 2) collect client-side latencies 3) export our server histogram samples for same time window.
Alex (Eng-SRE): quick snippet I ran to fetch our metric (Prometheus style):

```
# Panel query (approx):
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_inference_request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```

That plus downsampled rollups can produce weird step changes when most observations sit on one bucket boundary.
Jordan (Observability): additional detail: our ingest pipeline compresses histogram buckets per minute using fixed boundaries [0.01,0.05,0.1,0.2,0.5,1,2]. If latency moves from 0.18 to 0.22 then p95 can jump from 0.2 to 0.5 in the dashboard, but raw samples would show a small delta. I call this "quantile-flooring" when using coarse buckets.
Taylor (Support): ok that matches. Customer probably saw ~220ms p95 on server but client sees 420ms — why the client doubled?
Sam (Oncall): two plausible contributors: 1) client-side includes network egress and retries; 2) our logs indicate a short spike in retries from the model runner at 14:08 — some requests retried once which doubles observed client latency for those requests.
Alex (Eng-SRE): logs (snippet):

```
[14:08:12] runner: request id=xyz status=retry reason="KV cache miss + transient kernel OOM"
[14:08:12] runner: request id=xyz status=ok duration=210ms
```

A subset of requests retried -> adds ~200ms extra to those samples. If client p95 includes retries but our histogram is sampling post-retry or increments in different buckets it diverges.
Jordan (Observability): TL;DR multiple signals: coarse histogram buckets + intermittent retries + routing to slightly slower pool. These compound to show large apparent p95 gap between different views.
Taylor (Support): what immediate mitigation can we offer the customer and what do we do internally?
Sam (Oncall): immediate customer-facing actions: 1) explain mismatch and root causes (retries + bucket-flooring + pool routing) 2) offer to route them to pool-gpu-a (older pool) for a short test or enable dedicated reservation 3) open an incident ticket and set alert at 2x baseline p95 so we catch recurrence.
Alex (Eng-SRE): internal mitigations: - disable aggressive retry for kernel OOMs (change to single retry + jitter) - revert the small autoscale that moved some capacity at 14:05 (we already rolled back at 14:20) - add a short-term dashboard panel that queries raw summaries instead of downsampled rollups:

```
# use prometheus summary if we export summaries, or use rate of observation counts + cumulative sum of le buckets to compute percentile without 1m rollup
sum(rate(redwood_inference_request_duration_bucket[1m])) by (le)
```

Jordan (Observability): longer-term: 1) widen buckets or use finer-grained boundaries for latency-critical routes 2) store exemplars/trace ids with histogram points so we can correlate spikes to traces 3) update dashboard docs to annotate that rollups can cause quantile-flooring and include a recommended comparison workflow (raw traces + client histograms).
Taylor (Support): done — I've drafted the customer response explaining these points and a short test plan (route to pool-gpu-a for 30m). I'll send after you sign off.
Sam (Oncall): signoff. Also created an alert channel and temporary pager rule for org-acme if p95 > 300ms for 10m.
Alex (Eng-SRE): created ticket INF-8732 to track retry changes and rollout to canary tomorrow.
Jordan (Observability): I'll add an explainer note to the dashboard and create a variant panel that uses raw ingestion window for the next 48h so support and oncall can compare.
incidents-bot: incident INF-8731 created (observability: quantile-flooring + retry-induced tail) assigned to eng-sre, priority P2.
Taylor (Support): customer notified with test route; awaiting their telemetry. Will post results. :thumbsup:
Sam (Oncall): thanks team. keep logs/traces attached to ticket so we can close once customer telemetry aligns.
